answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, like a juniper seedling that only takes root after surviving a cold snap. One deposit buys one voice, so an attacker spawning a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand bonds, a glacier of frozen capital that melts only through honest work. A lone island of fake agents stays small because each new identity costs real money, while honest agents earn their bond back with fees.
